text: The New Hotspots universe should remain cross-sector and chokepoint-driven rather than collapsing into one ticker cluster; InP, HBM second-order suppliers, sulphur/acid, grid power, and nuclear fuel each need separate validation tracks.
InP substrates and InP laser manufacturing equipment are currently the strongest evidence-backed nodes, with AXTI and VECO ranking highest for Layer 1 relevance.
AI data-center power should be researched below the obvious leaders through switchgear, electrical balance-of-system, busways, enclosures, grid hardware, and construction-input suppliers.
Sulphur and sulphuric-acid disruption is a real theme-level chokepoint from provided evidence, but company-level public-market mapping remains weaker and must be validated asset by asset.
Layer 2 must refresh market caps, analyst coverage, liquidity, valuation, and primary filings before any candidate is considered underfollowed with high confidence.
Speculative_shadow candidates such as ASYS, ALMU, AAOI, AEHR, and SMR should survive only if direct customer, revenue, backlog, or contract evidence appears in primary sources.
Treat AI compute leaders, HBM producers, and optical-module leaders as demand anchors; do not let them dominate the New Hotspots map.

InP substrates and raw indium export-permit gates are high-priority chokepoint nodes for AI optical interconnects, with AXTI, COHR, LITE, and VECO as relevant mapping anchors rather than a completed investment ranking.
Advanced PCB substrate glass / T-glass appears to be a concentrated AI-buildout material node with process-knowledge and customer-qualification barriers.
HBM producers are high-attention and likely already priced as obvious beneficiaries; Layer 2A should focus on probe cards, inspection/metrology, process subsystems, and packaging yield-control tools.
Data-center electrical infrastructure may hide underfollowed bottlenecks in switchgear, grid interconnection, electrical rooms, conduit, enclosures, connectors, cable management, and copper wire.
Sulphur and sulphuric acid are non-AI New Hotspot chokepoints with downstream exposure to copper SX-EW, Indonesian HPAL nickel, fertilizer, industrial acid, and vessel-level trade-route shifts.

China sulphuric acid export ban through August 2026, China indium/InP export controls, AI optical 800G/1.6T ramps, advanced-glass capacity additions in 2026-2027, and data-center power interconnection demand are the main catalyst clusters to monitor.

Need primary-source verification for each company node: latest 10-K/10-Q, earnings-call transcripts, customer concentration, backlog, capacity timing, export-permit status, and revenue mix tied specifically to AI, HBM, optical, power, or sulphur-chain exposure.
Need to verify whether Encore Wire remains an investable public-market candidate because the cached Layer 1 universe flags current public status as a verification item.

Need more source work on distributors, certification labs, trade-route logistics firms, port operators, and inspection/testing providers; these may be hidden bottleneck nodes but are not yet adequately mapped from current evidence.

AXTI is the highest-priority underfollowed relationship in this chunk: direct InP substrate exposure, export-permit chokepoint, AI optics demand linkage, and explicit backlog/capacity signals make it the clearest Serenity bottleneck candidate, pending primary-source validation.

VECO should be tracked as a second-order InP capacity-enablement ticker rather than a direct optical demand name; promote only if backlog/orders clearly tie to InP lasers, photonics, or 800G/1.6T AI optical capacity.

COHR and LITE are reference anchors, not underfollowed alpha targets in this chunk; their primary role is to validate downstream AI optical demand and test whether vertical integration weakens independent substrate suppliers.

MKSI, FORM, and CAMT belong to the HBM/advanced-packaging second-order supplier lane, but all require revenue-materiality checks to distinguish true HBM/AI exposure from broad semiconductor cyclicality.

POWL and HUBB map to AI power-infrastructure and grid hardware, but the current evidence is node-level rather than company-specific; backlog composition and data-center project mix are the critical survival tests.

LEU is a regulated-input chokepoint candidate for nuclear fuel and HALEU, but its link to AI power demand is indirect and policy-dependent; keep as a watch-list hypothesis until DOE milestones, contracts, and capacity are verified.

Need primary-source filings and transcripts for AXTI, VECO, POWL, MKSI, FORM, CAMT, LEU, HUBB, COHR, and LITE before Layer 3 scoring; current evidence is strongest for the InP optical chain and weakest for AI power and nuclear-fuel ticker specificity.

Market-cap bucket, analyst coverage, liquidity, valuation, and recent price-action checks were not refreshed in this Layer 2B mapping and should be validated separately before any prioritization upgrade.

NVT maps to AI data-center electrical balance-of-system, enclosures, protection, and thermal-management infrastructure; relationship remains hypothesis-level until data-center sales mix, backlog, and product-level exposure are verified.

KLIC, BESI.AS, and ACMR map to the HBM/advanced-packaging second-order supplier lane; the key promotion test is whether orders and revenue are explicitly tied to HBM, AI accelerator packaging, hybrid bonding, or advanced packaging rather than generic semiconductor recovery.

AEHR maps to semiconductor reliability test and burn-in as a speculative_shadow candidate; downgrade quickly if AI optical, advanced-packaging, or power-device customer wins are absent and silicon-carbide cyclicality dominates.
ASYS maps to compound-semiconductor substrate processing and polishing as a speculative_shadow InP/photonic-tooling candidate; evidence must be collected at subsidiary and product-line level.

ALMU maps to possible InP substitution through compound-semiconductor-on-silicon photonics, but commercialization, customer, revenue, readiness, cash-runway, and dilution evidence are mandatory before further promotion.

AAOI maps to downstream AI optical interconnects and optical modules; it may be a beneficiary or bottleneck victim depending on 800G/1.6T product traction, laser/InP sourcing, and AI customer concentration.
FCX and SCCO should remain reference anchors for sulphuric-acid and copper-chain validation, not primary underfollowed alpha candidates.
Capstone Copper appears to map to underfollowed copper/SX-EW acid-supply sensitivity, but the candidate input was truncated and requires reconstruction from filings before scoring.
Layer 2B lacks refreshed market-cap, analyst-coverage, liquidity, valuation, and current-price context for the visible candidate chunk; these should be collected before Layer 2C prioritization.

Most ticker relationships are supported by node-level evidence rather than primary company evidence; next step should prioritize SEC filings, annual reports, investor decks, earnings transcripts, backlog, segment revenue, customer concentration, and product datasheets.
Sulphuric-acid disruption evidence is strong at the macro and trade-route level, but company-specific sensitivity for FCX, SCCO, and Capstone Copper remains unproven.

InP and optical-interconnect evidence is strong at the node level, but AAOI, ASYS, and ALMU require direct product/customer/revenue validation before they can survive beyond speculative_shadow status.

603799.SS should remain the strongest reference anchor in the sulphur-to-Indonesian-HPAL chain because external Kpler evidence directly links Huayou to an Indonesian output reduction amid sulphur feedstock stress.

NIC.AX remains an underfollowed hypothesis, not a confirmed chokepoint beneficiary; promotion requires issuer-level evidence of HPAL/MHP exposure, sulphur procurement sensitivity, and Indonesian project economics.

MOS and NTR currently have only theme-level sulphur/fertilizer linkage; Layer 3 should verify phosphate segment materiality, sulphuric-acid sourcing, pass-through ability, and whether disruption is large enough relative to nitrogen/potash/crop-price drivers.

UUUU and NXE are nuclear/uranium policy hypotheses, not direct AI-power chokepoints; next validation should focus on contract visibility, permitting, funding, production timelines, and whether policy support converts into issuer-level cash flows.

VRT, ETN, GEV, CEG, and CCJ should be treated as reference anchors rather than underfollowed targets; use their backlog, contract, and demand commentary to validate smaller suppliers or second-order beneficiaries.

AI data-center power names in this chunk need disaggregation between true AI-driven incremental backlog and broad electrification/grid modernization narratives before any underfollowed supplier mapping is promoted.
